content.text:
I found the cause. The game isn't failing to load ships at random: during startup it looks for every base-game file in the wrong folder.

**Where the logs are:**
- `drive_c/Program Files (x86)/Steam/steamapps/common/Sea Power/Sea Power_Data/Logs/2026-10-13_session_2.html` is the game's own session log (124 MB) and the useful one.
- `Player.log` (Unity) and `ScriptEngine.log` (the built-in web browser) in `AppData/LocalLow/Triassic Games/Sea Power/` contain nothing relevant.

**What the session log shows:**
- **Wrong folder at startup.** Right after "Loading unit metadata" (15:08:55), every unit, ammo, campaign, language and terrain file is looked up in `StreamingAssets\user\` (the "User Data" mod folder) instead of `StreamingAssets\original\` (the "Base Game" folder):
  ```
  ERROR: Could not find a part of the path "...\StreamingAssets\user\vessels\usn_ssn_los_angeles.ini" ... (from mod 'User Data')
  ERROR: usn_ssn_los_angeles: Unknown or missing unit role: ''
  ```
  `user\` only contains `_info.ini` and your missions. All the real files are in `original\`, and they're intact (about 7,600 files).
- **That gives the zero points.** The game records every unit as read from an empty file (503 of 555 units in `cache/taskforce_pointvalues.json` have the hash of empty input). `cache/pointvalues.csv` shows 521 of 573 units at cost 0, so no ships spawn and the task force builder shows zeros.
- **It started with today's update.** On Oct 2 (v0.8.3) there were no `user\` path errors. Today's first launch on v0.8.5 didn't finish loading, and the second produced about 153,000 of these errors, mostly terrain chunks once a mission started.
- **Later loading works.** After startup, the game reads files from `original\` correctly. So the fault is in how 0.8.5 decides which mod folder each file belongs to during the early loading phase. A web search found no reports of this exact problem. My best guess is a 0.8.5 bug that only shows up under Wine/CrossOver, but I couldn't confirm that because no .NET decompiler is installed here.

**What I'd try, in order (I haven't changed anything):**
1. **Delete the point cache:** remove `AppData/LocalLow/Triassic Games/Sea Power/cache/` so the zero values aren't reused. It's regenerated on launch.
2. **Verify game files in Steam,** although the game's own file check passed.
3. **Move the `user` folder aside for one launch:** rename `StreamingAssets/user` to `user.bak`. This tests whether the bad lookup only happens when that folder exists. Your custom missions are in it, so it's easy to undo.
4. **Roll back:** in Steam, under Properties → Betas, switch to a previous-version branch if Triassic offers one.
5. **Report it to Triassic Games** with one of the log lines above and the note that it started in 0.8.5 under CrossOver.

- [Unity Discussions: DirectoryNotFoundException for StreamingAssets on Mac](https://discussions.unity.com/t/directorynotfoundexception-for-streamingassets-on-mac/668728)

content.text:
Most likely yes, though the lack of reports is weaker evidence than it sounds.

**Why CrossOver is the main suspect:**
- If 0.8.5 did this on normal Windows, every player would get a game with no ships. That would be all over the Steam forums within a day or two.
- The broken part is the game deciding which mod folder owns each file, which depends on how the system answers "does this file exist?" and "list this folder". Wine reimplements exactly those Windows file APIs, so code that's new in 0.8.5 could easily behave differently under it.
- There's another Wine-flavoured error in the same log: clearing the campaign temp folder fails with "Unknown error (0x2f8d180)". That points to file operations not behaving the way the game expects.
- I've ruled out the external drive: it's standard case-insensitive APFS, which Wine handles fine.

**Caveats:**
- 0.8.5 came out on Oct 8, only five days ago. My single search didn't check the Steam forums or the game's Discord directly, and the Linux/Proton players most likely to hit the same thing could have reported it there.
- You're on CrossOver **Preview**, so a regression in the preview Wine build is as plausible as an incompatibility in the game.

**Ways to confirm:**
- Run the same game in a bottle under the stable (non-Preview) CrossOver release. If units load, it's the Preview build.
- Check the Sea Power Steam discussions for Proton/Steam Deck reports about 0.8.5. If Linux players see "no units" too, it's a Wine issue the developers can work around.
- Roll back to 0.8.4 through Steam betas if it's offered. If units load there under the same CrossOver, the trigger is the new 0.8.5 code combined with Wine.

If you report it to Triassic Games, say it's under CrossOver/Wine and include one of the `...\user\vessels\...` log lines. That points them straight at their file-to-folder lookup.
I tried normal before and did preview to see if it helps, going back to 0.8.2 works, 0.8.4 didn't either..

content.text:
That confirms CrossOver Preview itself isn't the cause. It does narrow down which build broke it.

**The regression window is one build.** Besides your 0.8.2 test, the Oct 2 log shows **0.8.3 (build 261001)** loading units with no `user\` path errors. So the break came in **0.8.4 build 261002**, released the next day. Its changelog has only two lines, and one is about the exact area that's failing:

```
02-Oct-2026: 0.8.4 Build 261002
[FIX] Mod menu folder picker not selecting directory
[FIX] Null refs and exceptions
```

Your log shows every file being assigned to the first mod folder ("User Data") instead of the one that actually contains it. A change to how mod directories are picked or resolved that also changed how mod roots are checked would explain that. It would also explain why it only breaks under Wine: Windows answers the existence or listing check one way, Wine another. That's an inference; I can't see the code. If you need a version to play on now, 0.8.3 is also known-good if Steam offers it.

**Next things worth trying:**
1. **Rename `StreamingAssets/user` to `user.bak` for one launch.** If the game then resolves files to `original\`, the bug is tied to how the first mod folder is checked. Put it back afterwards; your custom missions are in it.
2. **A workaround if that doesn't help:** if the game insists on reading from `user\`, make the files appear there. Symbolic links from `user/vessels`, `user/aircraft` and the other folders to the matching folders in `original/` would do it, and Wine follows these transparently. One catch: the `user` folder is synced to Steam Cloud, so disable Steam Cloud for Sea Power first, or it may try to upload the entire game data.
3. **Report it to Triassic Games:** "Since 0.8.4 build 261002, under CrossOver/Wine, every base-game file is resolved to `StreamingAssets\user\` instead of `original\`; 0.8.3 build 261001 works." Attach one of the log lines. The narrow build range should let them find the cause quickly.

I can set up the links for option 2 (it's easy to undo) or draft the bug report if you want.

content.text:
I didn't find any Proton reports of this exact problem, but the search turned up a lead worth testing.

**What the search found:**
- **Proton issue #9053** (Sept 2025): under Proton, Sea Power silently skipped loading its music when the Steam library path contained a dot, for example `~/.local/share/Steam`. It listed the files in a `StreamingAssets\user\...` folder correctly but never opened them. Valve fixed it with a launch option and a per-game override. So the game's file-path code has a history of breaking on odd characters in paths.
- **ProtonDB:** the page didn't load for me, and an aggregator summary only mentions general quirks and a few reports of it running fine.
- **Steam thread "Units not loading"** (Jan 2025): there's no platform, version or reply, so it's not useful here.

**The lead:** your path has no dots, so that exact bug doesn't apply here. But your install has something a Windows or Proton install wouldn't: **macOS Finder `.DS_Store` files** inside the game's data folders:

```
Sea Power_Data/StreamingAssets/.DS_Store
Sea Power_Data/StreamingAssets/original/.DS_Store
Sea Power_Data/StreamingAssets/original/audio/.DS_Store
(plus two higher up)
```

These appear when a folder is opened in Finder. Under Wine they look like ordinary files. If the 0.8.4 change to mod-folder handling scans the `original` folder and trips over a file with no name before the dot, the game could drop "Base Game" from its index and fall back to "User Data" for everything. That's exactly what your log shows. It would also explain why only you seem to hit it. It's a guess: they already existed when 0.8.3 worked, so this only holds if 0.8.4 changed how that folder is scanned.

It's a cheap, safe test: move those five `.DS_Store` files out of the game folder (they're only Finder view settings), delete `AppData/LocalLow/Triassic Games/Sea Power/cache/`, and launch 0.8.5. Avoid opening the game folders in Finder afterwards, or they'll come back. I can move them to a backup folder now so they're easy to restore. Want me to?

Sources:
- [ValveSoftware/Proton issue #9053: Sea Power](https://github.com/valvesoftware/proton/issues/9053)
- [ProtonDB: Sea Power](https://www.protondb.com/app/1286220)
- [Steam discussion: Units not loading](https://steamcommunity.com/app/1286220/discussions/0/507318096807121440/)
- [Steam discussion: proton possible?](https://steamcommunity.com/app/1286220/discussions/0/4631483574657232359/)
- [vaporlens.app Sea Power summary](https://vaporlens.app/app/1286220/sea_power_naval_combat_in_the_missile_age)
yes, but I installed the game and did start it and it directly failed, it's unlikely the folders were created at that point in time already, right?
Fair point. I'll check the files' exact creation times against the install and the first launch, rather than guess.

content.text:
You're right, and checking it showed I got something else wrong earlier.

**The `.DS_Store` files weren't created by Finder.** All five were created in the same second (Oct 2, 16:58:29), while Steam was still downloading and before your first launch at 16:59. The most likely explanation is that they ship in the game's Steam download: a developer on a Mac left them in the build. In that case Windows players have them too, so they're probably not the cause. The test is still harmless, but I don't expect much from it.

**Correction: 0.8.3 on Oct 2 was broken too.** I said it loaded fine because it had none of the `user\` path errors, but looking closer, the same failure is there:

```
usn_ffg_oliver_hazard_perry: Unknown or missing unit role: ''
Attempted to add unit from variant Default which does not exist ...
ObjectBaseLoader is unable to load resources root ''! Object will not be loaded
```

That's the same pattern as today: the unit files are read as empty. 0.8.3 just didn't log why, and later versions added the "Could not find a part of the path ...\user\..." error that shows the cause. That matches what you saw, broken from the first launch.

**So the regression is 0.8.2 → 0.8.3, not 0.8.3 → 0.8.4.** That throws out my "mod folder picker" theory. The 0.8.3 changelog only lists translations and a Phalanx tweak, so whatever changed file resolution wasn't announced. That's still useful for the bug report: "0.8.2 works under CrossOver, 0.8.3 and later read all base-game files from `StreamingAssets\user\`."

Given that, the symlink workaround (so `user/vessels` and the other folders point at `original/`) is probably the most practical way to play 0.8.5 until Triassic fixes it. I can set it up once you've turned off Steam Cloud for Sea Power, or write the bug report. Which would you prefer?
why do I need to turn off Steam Cloud?

The game's own `user/_info.ini` says that folder "is synchronised to Steam Cloud", and it contains a `steam_autocloud.vdf` marker. I'll check what Steam actually syncs from it so I'm not just guessing.

content.text:
Because that `user` folder is synced to Steam Cloud, recursively, and the workaround would put the whole game's data inside it.

**What Steam currently syncs for Sea Power** (from its `remotecache.vdf` in the bottle):

```
Sea Power_Data/StreamingAssets/user/_info.ini
Sea Power_Data/StreamingAssets/user/missions/user_missions/_info.ini
Triassic Games/Sea Power/saves/missions/New File.sav
```

It picks up files in subfolders of `user/`, not just the top level. The workaround would add links like `user/vessels → original/vessels`. Steam follows links like any other folder, so it would suddenly see thousands of new files. I can't see Steam's exact file-matching rule for this game, but its rules clearly include `.ini` files, and nearly all of the unit data is `.ini`. Two things could go wrong:

1. **Upload:** Steam would try to upload up to 4.9 GB of game data as your "save data". That probably exceeds the game's cloud quota, causing sync errors or a stuck "syncing" state at launch or exit.
2. **The worse one, later:** any other machine, or a reinstall, would download those files as real copies into `user/`. The game loads "User Data" first, as an override of the base game. After the next patch, those stale copies would quietly replace the updated unit data, creating a new hard-to-diagnose bug, possibly on a Windows PC where everything otherwise works.

Turning Cloud off for Sea Power only (Steam → Sea Power → Properties → General → "Keep game saves in the Steam Cloud") avoids both. The downside is that your saves and custom missions won't sync while it's off. Once Triassic fixes the bug, you'd remove the links first and then turn Cloud back on.

If you'd rather not touch Cloud, the bug report is the alternative, and you'd play 0.8.2 in the meantime.
hmm, but this makes the issue even more strange right, so it can be a wrong installation on my machine the lookup is completely false

It could be. If 0.8.3+ broke the lookup under Wine for everyone, Linux players would likely have reported it, so something specific to your setup is plausible. The lookup isn't just looking in the wrong place: it acts as if "User Data" contains every file. The first thing I'd check is the game's stored settings: Unity games keep preferences, which can include the mod list and load order, in the registry, and in a bottle that's `user.reg`.

content.text:
I can't find anything wrong with the installation itself. Everything specific to it checks out:

- **Game files:** all present (about 7,600 in `original/`), and the game's own validity check passes on every launch.
- **No mods:** no Workshop items and no extra mod folders. `user/` holds only the default `_info.ini`, your custom mission and the Steam Cloud marker.
- **Settings:** the registry has only screen and analytics values, and `usersettings.ini` has nothing about mods or file paths. There's no Sea Power data elsewhere in the bottle or in your Documents.
- **Same files, same session:** right after the bad lookups, the game reads the very same files from `original\` without trouble (the "IniHandler: reading '…/original/…'" lines). The files are fine. One particular lookup step gives the wrong answer.

So the input to that lookup is the same as on any Windows PC. What differs is the environment it runs in: Wine's versions of the Windows file APIs on a Mac filesystem. Wine imitates Windows but differs in small details, such as how it reports file attributes or orders directory listings. Code that leans on such a detail can work on real Windows and fail here. Since 0.8.2 works in the exact same bottle, something changed in 0.8.3 that relies on one of those details. That's the most consistent explanation, though without the game's code I can't name the detail.

Two tests can settle it:

1. **Fresh profile, same bottle:** rename `AppData/LocalLow/Triassic Games/Sea Power` and `StreamingAssets/user` to `.bak` and launch once. If it works, some leftover state was the trigger.
2. **Fresh bottle:** create a new CrossOver bottle, install Steam and Sea Power, and launch. If it fails the same way there, it's CrossOver on macOS plus 0.8.3 or later, not your machine's install. That's the most useful fact for the bug report.

I can do the renames for test 1 now; they're easy to undo.

The fresh profile made no difference, so leftover state isn't the cause.

**What this run shows:**
- With no profile, the game went straight into the intro mission, skipping the usual menu loading. Its units fail the same way: `usn_cg_belknap`, `usn_ddg_kidd`, `usn_ffg_oliver_hazard_perry_longhull` and the rest are read as empty, giving "Unknown or missing unit role: ''" and "unable to load resources root ''".
- Those unit failures come **without** any "could not find path" error. That's the same pattern as the 0.8.3 run on Oct 2. The `user\` lookup errors only appear later, for terrain (38,000 of them).
- So the path error isn't the root problem; it's another symptom. Base-game files are returned as empty or missing whichever way they're loaded. That fits the theory that something at the file-system level behaves differently under Wine, more than a bad mod lookup.

**What's left:**
- **Test 2, a fresh bottle,** would tell you whether this is specific to your bottle or to CrossOver on macOS in general. That takes a full Steam install and a game download of about 5 GB.
- **The bug report** has enough to send now. The key facts: 0.8.2 works, 0.8.3 and later read base-game files as empty under CrossOver/Wine, and it reproduces with a clean profile. I can draft it with the relevant log excerpts.

The game is still running. Quit it, then tell me whether to restore your original folders (settings, saves, custom mission) or keep the fresh ones. I'd restore them, since the fresh state didn't help.

content.text:
Your original folders are back: settings, saves, campaign progress and `_Custom Mission.ini` are all in place. I kept the folders from the test run as `Sea Power.fresh` (in `LocalLow/Triassic Games`) and `user.fresh` (in `StreamingAssets`); they only hold defaults and can be deleted whenever you like.

**Where this leaves things:**
- **Ruled out:** your profile, settings, the point cache, the `user` folder contents, CrossOver Preview versus the regular CrossOver release, and a broken or incomplete install.
- **Confirmed:** 0.8.2 works, while 0.8.3, 0.8.4 and 0.8.5 all read base-game files as empty under CrossOver, even with a completely fresh profile.
- **Cause:** almost certainly a change in 0.8.3's file loading that behaves differently under Wine on macOS. Without the game's code I can't pin down exactly what.

**Options from here:**
1. **Play 0.8.2** through the Steam betas until it's fixed. This is the dependable choice.
2. **Report it to Triassic Games** on the Steam forums, their Discord or their bug tracker. I can draft the report with the version range, the relevant log lines and the clean-profile result.
3. **Try a fresh bottle** if you want to rule out this particular bottle before reporting. It costs a Steam install and a 5 GB download.

I'd do 1 and 2 together. Want me to draft the report?
if I'd gave you a decompiler, what could you do?

Quite a lot. This is a good case for a decompiler: the game's logic is in `Sea Power_Data/Managed/Seapower-Scripts.dll`, which is ordinary .NET (Mono) code, so it decompiles back into readable C#, including the class and method names the log already points to (`FileManager.cs`, `IniHandler.cs`, `IniPreloader.cs`, `UnitMetadataProvider.cs`).

**What I'd do:**
1. **Read the lookup code.** Follow `IniHandler.ReadFileToIni` and `FileManager` to see how the game decides which mod folder a file belongs to, and why a base-game file can come back empty.
2. **Compare with 0.8.2.** If you also keep a copy of the 0.8.2 version of that DLL, which is easy to get from the Steam beta, I can compare the relevant code between versions. The regression is between 0.8.2 and 0.8.3, so the change responsible should stand out.
3. **Find the specific dependency on Windows behaviour.** For example, the code might rely on directory listings coming back in a certain order, on a particular file attribute, or on a check for the `\\?\` long-path prefix. One hint: the "Unable to clear temp files ... `\\?\C:\users...`" warning shows the game uses that prefix, and Wine's handling of it is a classic source of differences.

**What that would give you:**
- **A workaround,** if the cause is something you can influence from outside: a Wine registry setting, a DLL override, or a change to the folder layout.
- **A runtime patch,** if not. Sea Power runs on Mono, so a mod loader such as BepInEx with a small Harmony patch can replace the faulty method when the game starts, without modifying any game files. It's the most work, but it would let you play 0.8.5 now.
- **A precise bug report:** "line X in `FileManager` assumes Y, which Wine doesn't guarantee". Triassic would very likely fix it quickly, and it could go to CodeWeavers if the fault is on Wine's side.

**Caveats:**
- The game's EULA may prohibit reverse engineering. For diagnosing a bug on your own machine that's usually a non-issue in practice, but you should know about it.
- I can't promise a workaround. If the fault is deep in Wine's file system, the result might "only" be a precise bug report.

**The tool:** `ilspycmd` runs fine on macOS. You don't need to hand me anything: if you OK it, I'd install the .NET SDK via Homebrew (`brew install dotnet`) and then `dotnet tool install -g ilspycmd`, about 200 MB in total. I'd decompile into the scratchpad only, never into the game folder.

content.text:
I haven't found the cause yet, but I've narrowed it to one specific piece of code.

**How the game finds files since this version:**
- It searches the mod folders in order: `user` first, then `original`.
- `user` gets a plain check of each file on disk.
- `original` is no longer checked file by file. On first use, the game lists the entire `original` tree once and keeps that list as an in-memory index (`FileManager.IndexFor`). Every later lookup only asks "is this name in the list?"
- If a file isn't found anywhere, many loaders fail **silently** and the unit ends up with empty data. That matches your fresh-profile run exactly: units loaded empty, with no error at all.

**Most likely cause:** on your machine, that index for `original` ends up empty or doesn't match the names being asked for. When the list fails with an error, the game logs "could not index" and carries on with an empty list. That warning never appears in your logs, so the list itself seems to succeed, but its entries don't match what the game asks for.

**What I ruled out:**
- I ran a test inside your bottle with CrossOver Preview's Wine: it correctly reports `user\vessels\…` as missing and `original\vessels\…` as present. So Wine's basic file checks work.
- `user` and `original` are set up correctly, and nothing else (registry, settings, mods) feeds into this lookup.

The `user\` paths in the errors are a side effect of how some loaders fall back. I haven't fully traced that, and it doesn't change the diagnosis.

**One caveat:** I briefly started the regular (non-Preview) CrossOver against this bottle while setting up the test. It printed an error about creating or updating the bottle environment and exited, so it doesn't seem to have changed anything. Still, if the bottle behaves oddly, that's why.

**Two ways to confirm, both need your OK:**
1. **Compare with 0.8.2 (cheap).** Switch Steam to 0.8.2 for a moment and I'll copy its `Seapower-Scripts.dll` to the scratchpad. Then switch back. Comparing the file-lookup code shows whether this index is what changed in 0.8.3.
2. **Look inside the running game (decisive).** I'd install BepInEx, a standard Unity mod loader, into the game folder. It needs a DLL override setting in the bottle. I'd add a tiny plugin that logs what the index actually contains at startup. That shows the exact mismatch, and the same plugin could then patch the lookup so you can play 0.8.5. It's all removable by deleting the BepInEx files and the override.

I'd start with 1. Shall I?

Confirmed. In 0.8.2, `GetFile` simply checks every mod folder with `File.Exists`:

```csharp
// 0.8.2
string text = Path.Join(Directories[i].DirectoryInfo.FullName, path);
if (File.Exists(text)) return text;
```

The cached file index (`_fileIndex`, `IndexFor`, `FileExistsIn`) doesn't exist in 0.8.2 at all; it was added later. So the change that breaks it for you is that index: the version that works checks files directly, and the versions that fail look them up in the index. The code is identical on Windows and in your bottle, so what the index ends up containing under Wine must differ from what it contains on Windows.

What I can't tell from reading the code is **why** the index comes out wrong here. The listing itself succeeds, since no warning gets logged, and Wine's basic file checks are correct. So the mismatch is in what the listing returns or how the game converts those entries to relative names inside the game's Mono runtime. Only running code inside the game can show that.

3. I write a small plugin that logs, at startup, what the index for `original` contains: entry count, sample entries, and the lookup for one unit file.

If the mismatch is what I expect, the same plugin can then switch the lookup back to plain `File.Exists`, which is exactly the 0.8.2 behaviour, letting you play 0.8.5 until Triassic fixes it. Removing it means deleting the BepInEx files and the override. Shall I go ahead once you're back on 0.8.5?

The plugin is written, built and installed. It's ready to test.

**What's installed** (all new files; nothing in the game was overwritten):
- In the game folder: `winhttp.dll`, `doorstop_config.ini`, `.doorstop_version` and the `BepInEx/` folder (BepInEx 5.4.23.5).
- The plugin: `BepInEx/plugins/SeaPowerFileIndexFix.dll`.
- In the bottle's registry: a `winhttp` DLL override that applies to `Sea Power.exe` only, so Steam isn't affected.

**What the plugin does:** it hooks three of the game's file-lookup methods and writes to `BepInEx/LogOutput.log`:
- For each mod folder the index is built for: how many entries it has, the first 8, whether it contains `vessels/usn_ssn_los_angeles.ini`, and how many files a fresh listing of the same folder finds right now.
- For the first 60 lookups: which folder was checked, the result, and what a direct `File.Exists` says.
- The optional fix (`UseFileExistsInsteadOfIndex`) is **off** for now, so this run only diagnoses and the game behaves as before.

content.text:
The first diagnostic run worked, and it disproved my theory. The improved version is now installed for a second run.

**What run 1 showed:**
- **The index is fine.** It has all 7,623 files in `original`, including `vessels/usn_ssn_los_angeles.ini`, and matches a fresh listing of the folder.
- **Lookups through `GetFile` are fine.** Every one I logged first checks `user` (correctly "not there") and then resolves to `original`.
- **The bug still happened in the same run:** 34,042 `user\` path errors and 527 units loaded empty.

So the bad `user\` paths don't come from the lookup I suspected; some other code builds them. My logging limit of 60 lookups ran out on audio files before units started loading, so it didn't catch which code.

**What the new version logs:**
- Any lookup that resolves into the `user` folder, with a stack trace for the first few.
- Any attempt to read a nonexistent file under `user\`, with the full stack trace showing exactly which code built that path.
- A few unit lookups (`vessels/`, `aircraft/`, `land_units/`) for comparison.

The first run's log is saved in the scratchpad. The fix switch stays off.

**About the exit hang:** it's probably related to BepInEx. Some mod-loader versions keep a background thread alive at shutdown with newer Unity versions. If it bothers you after we're done, removing BepInEx will fix it.

Please launch once more, wait until you reach the main menu (that's enough, since units load during startup), and quit.
quick question: could it be that the paths are somehow mac+wine special and that is an issue? anyway, doing the second launch now

Possibly, but less likely now than it seemed earlier. Inside the bottle the game only ever sees Windows-style paths (`C:\Program Files (x86)\...`); Wine translates them to Mac paths underneath. In run 1, everything the plugin could observe behaved like Windows: `File.Exists`, folder listings, and conversion to relative names all gave correct results, and the Mac-specific traits like case-insensitivity match Windows anyway. The only Mac artifact was the `.DS_Store` entry in the index, which does no harm.

I now have a different suspect: **timing**. The `user\` errors come in bursts within the same millisecond, while units load in parallel on several threads. The game runs as x86 code translated by Rosetta inside Wine, so threads interleave very differently from a native Windows PC. If two threads share a cache that isn't safe for that (`IniHandler` has several static ones), a race that almost never shows up on Windows could happen reliably here. That would also explain why the failures differ a little between runs. The stack traces from this launch should show whether the bad paths come from such parallel code.

I'll read the log once you've quit.

content.text:
I found the cause, and a fix is installed but hasn't been tested in a game run yet.

**What's happening:** since 0.8.3, the game loads unit and ammunition files on many threads at once. For each file it first asks "is there a copy in the `user` folder?" using `File.Exists`. When the game runs under CrossOver, that check sometimes answers "yes" for files that don't exist, and only on those parallel threads. The game then tries to read the nonexistent `user\vessels\...` file and fails, and the unit ends up with no data: zero points and no ships. On Windows the check is reliable, which is why nobody else reports this. 0.8.2 works because it loaded everything on a single thread.

The evidence is direct: the second diagnostic run logged `File.Exists = True` for missing files on worker threads 6, 9, 10, 15 and 17–23, while the same check on the main thread gave the right answer.

**The fix (plugin 1.1.0):** before the game trusts a "yes" for the `user` folder, the plugin confirms it with a directory listing, which behaved correctly in both runs. It only changes the answer when the check was wrong, and logs a line like `Rejected false File.Exists for ...` whenever it catches one. The setting is `VerifyFileExists` in `BepInEx/config/local.seapower.fileindexfix.cfg`, on by default.

I also moved the point-value cache, which still holds the zero values, to `cache.zero-points.bak` so the game rebuilds it.

**Please launch once more** and check the task force builder and a mission. If ships appear with real point values, it works. I'll then check the logs for the rejected-check counts and for any remaining `user\` errors. If some remain, other parallel code paths do their own `File.Exists` checks and I'd extend the plugin to cover them.

Rolling back takes three steps: delete `winhttp.dll`, `doorstop_config.ini`, `.doorstop_version` and `BepInEx/` from the game folder, and remove the `winhttp` override for `Sea Power.exe`. That also cures the exit hang. I can do it whenever you want.
this theory makes sense since sometimes it loads with a single unit available

Yes, that fits. A race like this doesn't hit every file the same way: which lookups get the false "yes" depends on how the threads happen to overlap in that particular launch. Your own logs show the same pattern: the Oct 2 run (0.8.3) had only 8 broken units, today's runs had 500+, and the fresh-profile run only broke the 18 units its mission used. Occasionally a unit slips through with a correct answer and loads normally, which would be the single working unit you've seen.

This variation is also why one good launch won't prove the fix. The decisive signs are in the logs: `Rejected false File.Exists` lines in `BepInEx/LogOutput.log` (the fix caught wrong answers), and zero `user\` path errors in the game's session log. Let me know when you've launched and I'll check both.

| | Before the fix | With plugin 2.0 |

**The remaining 13 errors are unrelated.** Your save's ships carry three helicopters (`rn_wasp_has1`, `rn_lynx_has2`, `raf_scout_ah1`) that don't exist anywhere in 0.8.5's game data, not even the unit files themselves. The save probably comes from a version that had them. There's also one "Plotting Table … type hash" error, which looks like the same old-save incompatibility. Nothing to do with CrossOver.

**What's installed now:**
- The game folder has BepInEx (`winhttp.dll`, `doorstop_config.ini`, `.doorstop_version`, `BepInEx/`) and the plugin `BepInEx/plugins/SeaPowerFileIndexFix.dll`. These survive Steam updates and file verification, and the plugin doesn't depend on any particular game version.
- The bottle has a `winhttp` DLL override for `Sea Power.exe` only.
- The plugin source is in the scratchpad (`plugin/Plugin.cs`), which is temporary. Tell me if you want it copied somewhere permanent.
- The game still hangs on exit with BepInEx, so force-quitting stays necessary for now.

**Cleanup you can do whenever you like:**
- In the game data folders: `Sea Power.fresh`, `user.fresh` and `cache.zero-points.bak` are leftovers from the tests and safe to delete.
- On the Mac, outside the bottle: I installed `dotnet` via Homebrew plus `ilspycmd`. Run `brew uninstall dotnet` and `rm -rf ~/.dotnet/tools` if you don't want to keep them.
- Once Triassic ships a fix, remove the BepInEx files and the override. I can do that in one step.

**Worth telling Triassic:** the cause is now precise enough to give them. "Under CrossOver/Wine, `File.Exists` returns true for nonexistent files when called from worker threads during `Parallel.For` in `UnitMetadataProvider.OnStart` / `IniPreloader` / terrain loading. `FileManager.FileExistsIn` checks the `user` folder with `File.Exists` first, so every unit resolves to `StreamingAssets\user\...` and loads empty. Single-threaded loading in 0.8.2 works." A simple fix on their side would be to also index the `user` folder, or to do the existence checks on the main thread. - Put the trimmed log excerpts (a few hundred lines each), `usersettings.ini`, and a short write-up of the diagnosis in one gist, then link it from the Steam post. A gist can hold several files, renders text nicely, and the developers can read it without downloading anything.
- Gists aren't meant for the raw 30–120 MB logs: GitHub truncates large files in the web view. Trimmed excerpts are more useful to the developers anyway. If they ask for full logs, you can upload those separately.
- Gists are public unless you make them "secret", which only means unlisted (anyone with the link can read them). The logs contain your Windows user path inside the bottle (`C:\users\crossover\...`) and the hardware details; I'd check them for anything personal before uploading. I didn't see anything sensitive in the parts I read.

**A repo for the plugin, if you want to help other players.** Probably worth it:
- Anyone on CrossOver, and possibly Proton or Steam Deck, with no units or broken terrain can use it until Triassic fixes the bug. The June terrain thread suggests you aren't the only one.
- Your bug report can link to it, which shows the developers exactly which check fixes it. That makes the fix on their side nearly trivial.
- It's small: one C# file, the `.csproj`, a README with install steps (BepInEx, the `winhttp` override in CrossOver, removal), an MIT license, and a release with the built DLL.
- **Important:** only your own plugin code goes in, never the decompiled game code. The README should describe the problem in terms of observed behaviour.
- Expect a little maintenance: people may open issues, and it becomes obsolete once Triassic fixes the bug. Saying so in the README ("temporary workaround until fixed upstream") sets the right expectation.

**How I'd go about it:** I prepare everything locally first: the repo folder with README, license and source; the gist files with trimmed logs; and the Steam post text. You review it all, and then either you publish it or I push with `gh`. Nothing goes public before you've seen it.

input.content:
# Sea Power CrossOver fix

A small [BepInEx](https://github.com/BepInEx/BepInEx) plugin that makes [Sea Power: Naval Combat in the Missile Age](https://store.steampowered.com/app/1286220/) load its units and terrain correctly when it runs under CrossOver (and possibly other Wine-based setups such as Proton).

This is a temporary workaround until the issue is fixed in the game itself. It does not modify any game files and contains no game code.

## Symptoms

Since version 0.8.3, under CrossOver on macOS:

- Missions start without ships, or with only a few of them.
- The campaign task force builder lists ships, but every unit costs 0 points.
- Terrain can be missing, with airfields and installations floating on water.
- The game's session log (`Sea Power_Data\Logs\*.html`) is full of errors like:

```
ERROR: Could not find a part of the path "...\Sea Power_Data\StreamingAssets\user\vessels\usn_ssn_los_angeles.ini". while parsing Ini File ... (from mod 'User Data')
ERROR: usn_ssn_los_angeles: Unknown or missing unit role: ''
```

Version 0.8.2 works fine in the same setup.

## Cause

Since 0.8.3 the game loads unit, ammunition and terrain data on many threads in parallel. For every file it first checks whether a user override exists in `StreamingAssets\user\` using `File.Exists`. Under CrossOver/Wine, `File.Exists` sometimes returns `true` for files that do not exist when it is called from those worker threads; on the main thread the same check answers correctly. The game then tries to read the base-game files from the nearly empty `user` folder, fails, and the units end up without data.

This was confirmed by logging the calls in a running game: in one session the plugin rejected about 2,700 false positives, all on worker threads.

## What the plugin does

It patches `System.IO.File.Exists`. Whenever the answer is `true` for a path inside the game's `StreamingAssets` folder, the plugin confirms it with a directory listing, which stays reliable, and turns the answer into `false` if the file is not really there. Paths outside `StreamingAssets` are not touched.

## Installation (CrossOver on macOS)

1. Download [BepInEx 5.4.23.5 for Windows x64](https://github.com/BepInEx/BepInEx/releases/tag/v5.4.23.5) (`BepInEx_win_x64_5.4.23.5.zip`) and unpack its contents into the game folder, next to `Sea Power.exe`. In a CrossOver bottle that is `drive_c/Program Files (x86)/Steam/steamapps/common/Sea Power/`.
2. Download `SeaPowerFileExistsFix.dll` from the [releases](../../releases) and put it into `BepInEx/plugins/` inside the game folder (create the folder if it does not exist).
3. Tell Wine to load BepInEx's `winhttp.dll` for the game. In CrossOver, open the bottle's Wine Configuration, go to Applications, add `Sea Power.exe`, then on the Libraries tab add `winhttp` and set it to "Native then Builtin". Alternatively, run this from Terminal (adjust the bottle name):

   ```sh
   "/Applications/CrossOver.app/Contents/SharedSupport/CrossOver/bin/wine" --bottle Steam reg add 'HKCU\Software\Wine\AppDefaults\Sea Power.exe\DllOverrides' /v winhttp /t REG_SZ /d native,builtin /f
   ```

4. Start the game. `BepInEx/LogOutput.log` in the game folder should contain a line like `Verifying File.Exists under '.../StreamingAssets/': True`, followed by `Rejected false File.Exists for ...` warnings once data loads.

If the campaign point values were already cached as 0, delete the `cache` folder in `AppData/LocalLow/Triassic Games/Sea Power/` inside the bottle so the game recomputes them.

For Proton, the usual BepInEx setup should apply (launch option `WINEDLLOVERRIDES="winhttp=n,b" %command%`). This has not been tested.

## Configuration

`BepInEx/config/soph.seapower.fileexistsfix.cfg` has a single switch, `VerifyFileExists` (default `true`), to turn the fix off without uninstalling it.

## Known issues

With BepInEx installed, the game may not quit properly from its own menu under CrossOver. Quitting it from macOS (Quit in the Dock, or Force Quit) works.

## Uninstall

Delete `winhttp.dll`, `doorstop_config.ini`, `.doorstop_version` and the `BepInEx` folder from the game folder, and remove the `winhttp` override for `Sea Power.exe` again.

## Building

Requires the .NET SDK and a Sea Power install with BepInEx 5 already set up (the build references the game's and BepInEx's assemblies from there):

```sh
dotnet build src -c Release -p:GameDir="/path/to/Sea Power"
```

The plugin ends up in `src/bin/Release/netstandard2.1/SeaPowerFileExistsFix.dll`.

## License

MIT, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Not affiliated with Triassic Games.

# Sea Power ≥ 0.8.3 under CrossOver: units load empty (no ships, 0 points)

## Summary

Since 0.8.3, Sea Power running under CrossOver on macOS (Wine) loads most units without data: missions start without ships, the campaign task force builder shows every unit at 0 points, and terrain can be missing. 0.8.2 works in the same bottle. The cause is that `File.Exists` returns `true` for nonexistent files when it is called from the worker threads of the new parallel loading code, so the game resolves base-game files to `StreamingAssets\user\...` and then fails to read them.

## Environment

- Sea Power 0.8.5 (build 261008), also seen with 0.8.3 (build 261001) and 0.8.4. 0.8.2 works.
- CrossOver 26 and CrossOver Preview on macOS (Apple Silicon, Mac16,9), Steam inside the bottle.
- No mods, no Workshop items. Reproduces with a fresh profile (LocalLow folder and `StreamingAssets\user` renamed before launch).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Run Sea Power ≥ 0.8.3 under CrossOver.
2. Open the campaign task force builder, or start any mission.
3. Units show 0 points / ships are missing. The session log contains thousands of `Could not find a part of the path "...\StreamingAssets\user\vessels\<unit>.ini" ... (from mod 'User Data')` followed by `<unit>: Unknown or missing unit role: ''`.

## Analysis

- The errors happen while `UnitMetadataProvider.OnStart` loads unit metadata in a `Parallel.For`, and also from `IniPreloader` and terrain loading.
- The `original\` file index is complete (7,623 entries, including all unit files).
- For the `user` folder, `FileManager.FileExistsIn` uses `File.Exists`. On the main thread this correctly returns `false` for missing files. On the `Parallel.For` worker threads it returns `true` for files that do not exist (the folders `user\vessels`, `user\aircraft` and `user\land_units` do not exist at all), so `GetFile` returns a path under `user\`, and reading it fails. See `3-file-exists-true-on-worker-threads.txt`, including a call stack.
- The terrain loader also chooses between `user\terrain\data\` and `original\terrain\data\` with `File.Exists`, which produces the same kind of errors for `chunk_*.dat` files once a mission loads.
- Plain Wine file checks from a single thread (e.g. `cmd /c if exist`) answer correctly in the same bottle.

## Workaround

A BepInEx plugin that confirms every positive `File.Exists` answer inside `StreamingAssets` with a directory listing fixes it completely: 0 `user\` path errors and 0 empty units, with about 2,700 false positives rejected in one session (`4-session-with-workaround.txt`). Source: <REPO_URL>

Possible fixes on the game side: also index the `user` folder (and invalidate the index when files are written there), or resolve file locations on the main thread before the parallel loading starts.

## Files

- `1-broken-session-0.8.5.txt`: session log excerpt, normal profile, no plugin.
- `2-broken-session-fresh-profile.txt`: the same with a fresh profile.
- `3-file-exists-true-on-worker-threads.txt`: diagnostic logging showing `File.Exists` results per thread, with a call stack.
- `4-session-with-workaround.txt`: session log excerpt with the workaround plugin.
- `Player.log`, `usersettings.ini`: from `AppData\LocalLow\Triassic Games\Sea Power\`, as requested in the pinned bug report post. (`Player.log` is from a session with the workaround installed; it contains nothing relevant either way.)

The full session logs (30–120 MB each) are available on request.

Title: [0.8.3+] Under CrossOver/Wine units load empty (no ships, 0 points) – File.Exists returns true on parallel loading threads

Since 0.8.3, Sea Power running under CrossOver on macOS loads most units without data: missions start without ships, the campaign task force builder shows every unit at 0 points, and terrain can be missing. 0.8.2 works fine in the same bottle. It reproduces with a fresh profile and without any mods, on 0.8.3, 0.8.4 and 0.8.5 (build 261008), with both CrossOver 26.3 and CrossOver Preview.

The session log is full of errors like: Could not find a part of the path "...\StreamingAssets\user\vessels\usn_ssn_los_angeles.ini" ... (from mod 'User Data'), followed by "usn_ssn_los_angeles: Unknown or missing unit role: ''".

I tracked it down with some logging: when unit metadata is loaded in parallel (UnitMetadataProvider.OnStart, also IniPreloader and the terrain loader), File.Exists returns true for files that don't exist when it's called from the worker threads. On the main thread it answers correctly. So the check for a user override in StreamingAssets\user succeeds for every unit, the game tries to read e.g. user\vessels\<unit>.ini, which doesn't exist, and the unit ends up empty. The original\ file index itself is complete.

As a workaround I wrote a small BepInEx plugin that double-checks positive File.Exists results inside StreamingAssets against a directory listing. With it, the game loads everything correctly (0 user\ path errors, 0 empty units, about 2,700 false positives caught per session): [REPO_URL]

Log excerpts, a call stack, usersettings.ini and Player.log are here: [GIST_URL]

Possible fixes on your side would be to index the user folder as well, or to resolve file locations on the main thread before the parallel loading starts. This probably also affects Proton / Steam Deck players, and may be what's behind the older thread "Terrain not appearing while using crossover": https://steamcommunity.com/app/1286220/discussions/0/567038259400789960/

Happy to test a fix or provide full logs.

3. Tell Wine to load BepInEx's `winhttp.dll` for the game. In CrossOver, open the bottle's Wine Configuration, go to Applications, add `Sea Power.exe`, then on the Libraries tab add `winhttp` and set it to "Native then Builtin". Alternatively, run this from Terminal (adjust the bottle name):
